segments.text: Why does a hundred dollars snowball over time?
Put a hundred dollars in the bank at ten percent a year. After one year, you have one hundred ten.
In year two, you earn ten percent on one hundred ten. That extra dollar is interest on interest.
Like a snowball rolling downhill, it picks up more snow with every turn, so it grows faster and faster.
So start early. Forty years of growth beats thirty by more than two and a half times.
Start early, and let time do the work.
